name: start_recording
description: Start a screen recording (Windows gdigrab) as a background ffmpeg process. Returns a session id and output path. Recording is explicit and never auto-starts. Audio is video-only by default; set audio.source = system to also capture loopback audio (needs a virtual-audio device; microphone capture is not supported). A window: target records the on-screen rectangle the window occupies, resolved once at start (window must be visible, on top, not minimized); it does not follow a window moved/resized mid-recording.

target.description: full | monitor:<index> (0 = primary) | window:<title> | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>. window: captures the rectangle the window occupies as displayed (case-insensitive exact title, else substring; topmost match)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match only a window whose title equals the given title (case-insensitive); never fall back to a substring (default false)

audio.description: Audio capture (default none, video-only). source system needs a loopback device; microphone capture is not supported.

source.description: system captures what is playing on the machine; none is video-only

device.description: Optional dshow loopback device name (from list_audio_devices); auto-detected when omitted

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

maxDurationSec.description: Stop automatically after this many seconds, finalizing the file (default 3600, or SCREENCAST_MAX_RECORDING_SEC). 0 = no cap

name: stop_recording
description: Stop a recording by session id. Sends ffmpeg a graceful quit so the file is finalized rather than truncated, then returns the final path and duration.

name: list_sessions
description: List all recording sessions (active and finished) with their status, target, output path, and whether the process is still alive.

name: get_session
description: Inspect a single recording session by id, including live status and whether its output file exists on disk.

name: screenshot
description: Capture a single still frame (PNG) of a target (full screen, a monitor, a window, or a region). Returns the image path, plus the image inline so the model can view it directly. A window: target captures the on-screen rectangle the window occupies as currently displayed (it must be visible, on top, and not minimized).

target.description: full | monitor:<index> | window:<title> | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>. window: captures the rectangle the window occupies as displayed (case-insensitive exact title, else substring; topmost match)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match only a window whose title equals the given title (case-insensitive); never fall back to a substring (default false)

backend.description: gdigrab (default) captures what is visible; wgc (window: targets, FFmpeg 8+) captures the window itself even when covered, via Windows Graphics Capture

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

returnImage.description: Also return the screenshot inline as a downscaled JPEG image (default true)

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale the inline image to at most this width (default 1280)

name: sample_frames
description: Sample frames from a video so the agent can view what happened: at a fixed rate (fps), at explicit timestamps, or only where the screen changed (mode scenes). Writes PNG frames to a folder and returns their paths, plus the first few frames inline so the model can view them directly.

input.description: Path to the source video file

mode.description: How to pick frames; scenes returns only frames where the screen changed (plus the first), strongest first up to maxFrames. Defaults to fps or timestamps, whichever is given

fps.description: Sample this many frames per second (mode fps)

timestamps.description: Explicit second offsets to grab one frame at each (mode timestamps)

sceneThreshold.description: Mode scenes: how much a frame must change to count, 0-1 (default 0.1)

dedupe.description: Mode fps: drop frames nearly identical to the previous one (default false)

outputDir.description: Optional folder for the frames (defaults under SCREENCAST_HOME/frames)

maxFrames.description: Most frames this call may write (default 100, max 1000); in fps mode a rate that would exceed it is lowered so frames still span the whole video

returnImages.description: Also return frames inline as downscaled JPEG images (default true)

maxInlineImages.description: How many frames to embed inline (default 8, max 20); every frame is still listed by path

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale inline images to at most this width (default 1280)

name: contact_sheet
description: Tile timestamped frames of a video into one image so the agent can see a whole recording in a single look: evenly spaced, or at the scene changes. Returns the image path and the sheet inline. poster: true writes a single representative frame instead.

count.description: How many frames to tile (default 12, max 48)

mode.description: even spreads frames across the video (default); scenes uses the opening frame plus the strongest scene changes

sceneThreshold.description: Mode scenes: how much a frame must change to count (default 0.1)

columns.description: Tiles per row (default: one row up to 4 tiles, then roughly square)

tileWidth.description: Width of each tile in px (default 320)

poster.description: Write one representative poster frame instead of a sheet

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

returnImage.description: Also return the sheet inline as a downscaled JPEG image (default true)

maxImageWidth.description: Downscale the inline image to at most this width (default 1280)

name: screen_diff
description: Compare two screenshots or frames: returns an SSIM similarity score, the share of the image that changed, and bounding boxes of the changed areas in b's pixel coordinates, plus b inline with those areas outlined. Use it to check that a UI change happened, and only where expected.

a.description: The before image (or video: its first frame)

b.description: The after image (or video); scaled to a's size if it differs

pixelThreshold.description: How different (0-255 mean per 8 px cell) an area must be to count as changed (default 12)

returnImage.description: Also return b inline with changed regions outlined (default true)

name: wait_for_change
description: Watch part of the screen and return when it changes (mode change) or when it has stopped changing (mode settle), instead of guessing a sleep. Reports how long it took, where the screen changed, and the final state as an inline screenshot.

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match the title exactly (default false)

mode.description: change (default): return when the target differs from the start; settle: return once it has stopped changing for settleSec

timeoutSec.description: Give up after this many seconds (default 30, max 600); a timeout is a normal result

settleSec.description: Mode settle: how long the screen must stay still (default 1)

pixelThreshold.description: How different an 8 px cell must be to count as changed (default 12)

returnImage.description: Also return a screenshot of the final state inline (default true)

name: find_text
description: Read text on screen or in an image/video frame with the OCR engine built into Windows (no install), with each line's and match's bounding box. Find where a label or button is, check what the screen says, or locate secrets and get redact_region rectangles for them. Best-effort detection: always review.

target.description: Read live from the screen: full | monitor:<index> | window:<title> | region:<x>,<y>,<w>,<h> (one of target / input)

input.description: Or read from an image or video file

timestamp.description: For a video input: the second to read (default 0)

exactTitle.description: For window: targets, match the title exactly (default false)

backend.description: For a live target: gdigrab (default) reads what is visible; wgc (window: targets, FFmpeg 8+) reads the window itself even when covered

query.description: Text to look for; case-insensitive and tolerant of OCR misreads (_ vs -, I vs l, O vs 0)

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression

redact.description: Also return padded rectangles around matches, ready for redact_region

returnImage.description: Return the image inline with matches outlined (default true when there is a query)

name: get_media_info
description: Probe a media file with ffprobe and return duration, resolution, frame rate, codecs, container format, and size.

input.description: Path to the media file to probe

name: trim
description: Trim a video to a sub-clip by start + (end or duration). Uses stream copy for speed; cut points snap to the nearest keyframe.

end.description: End time in seconds (use end OR duration)

duration.description: Clip length in seconds (use end OR duration)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: concat
description: Concatenate two or more videos into a single file using the ffmpeg concat demuxer (stream copy). Inputs should share the same codec and format.

inputs.description: Two or more video paths to join, in order

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: convert
description: Convert a video between mp4, gif, and webm. mp4 uses H.264, webm uses VP9, and gif uses a palette filter for quality. Returns the output path.

width.description: Output width in px, height auto (gif only; default 720)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: export_gif
description: Export a video as an optimized animated GIF or WebP that fits a file-size budget (default: GitHub's 10 MB image limit), for PRs, issues, and READMEs. Steps fps, width, and palette/quality down until it fits and reports the settings used.

format.description: gif (default) or webp (animated WebP, usually much smaller)

start.description: Start at this many seconds into the video

duration.description: Export only this many seconds (default: to the end)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: crop
description: Crop a video to a pixel rectangle (x, y, width, height) and re-encode. A rectangle that runs off the source frame is rejected rather than silently clamped.

x.description: Left edge of the crop in pixels

y.description: Top edge of the crop in pixels

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: scale
description: Resize a video to a target width and/or height and re-encode. Provide one side to keep the aspect ratio, or both for an exact size.

width.description: Target width in px (omit to derive from height)

height.description: Target height in px (omit to derive from width)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: speed
description: Change playback speed by a factor (>1 faster, <1 slower) and re-encode. Audio is retempo'd to match when the source has an audio track.

factor.description: Speed multiplier: >1 faster, <1 slower (2 = double speed)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: overlay
description: Composite an image or video (logo, watermark, picture-in-picture) onto a base video at a pixel position, optionally scaled and time-limited.

overlay.description: Path to the overlay image or video

width.description: Optional overlay width in px (height auto)

height.description: Optional overlay height in px (width auto)

start.description: Optional second to show the overlay from

end.description: Optional second to hide the overlay after

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: callout
description: Annotate a video with timed boxes, text labels, and arrows (e.g. a box around the bug, 'click here'), each shown between two timestamps. Returns the output path.

items.description: Annotations drawn in order (later on top). box: {type, x, y, width, height, thickness?, fill?}; text: {type, x, y, text, size?, background?}; arrow: {type, x1, y1, x2, y2 (head), thickness?}. All take from?, to? (seconds) and color?

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: compress
description: Re-encode a video to a smaller file with a CRF quality ladder (light/medium/heavy) and an optional width cap that only downscales.

maxWidth.description: Optional width cap in px; only ever downscales

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: extract_audio
description: Extract the audio track of a media file to its own file (mp3, aac, wav, or copy). Returns the output path.

format.description: Audio output codec; copy keeps the source codec without re-encoding

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: normalize_audio
description: Normalize a recording's loudness to a delivery target (EBU R128, two-pass loudnorm) so narration and system audio are neither too quiet nor clipping. Video is copied untouched. Reports the loudness before and after.

input.description: Path to the source video or audio file

target.description: youtube (-14 LUFS, default), podcast (-16), broadcast (EBU R128, -23), or a LUFS number such as -18

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: denoise
description: Reduce steady background noise (fan, hum, hiss) in a recording's audio with an adaptive FFT denoiser tuned to the file's measured noise floor. Video is copied untouched.

input.description: Path to the source video or audio file

strength.description: How hard to reduce noise: light (6 dB), medium (12 dB, default), strong (20 dB)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: transcribe
description: Transcribe a recording's speech to an SRT subtitle file, locally, with FFmpeg 8's whisper filter (needs a whisper.cpp model file). Returns the SRT path and the text. Pair with burn_subtitles to caption the video.

input.description: Path to the video or audio to transcribe

model.description: Path to a whisper.cpp model file (ggml-*.bin); defaults to SCREENCAST_WHISPER_MODEL

language.description: Spoken language code, e.g. en, or auto (default)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: burn_subtitles
description: Burn subtitles (an SRT from transcribe, or any SRT/ASS) permanently into a video, in the bundled font, in a clean or social-media style. Returns the output path.

subtitles.description: Path to an .srt or .ass subtitle file

style.description: clean (default): a modest outlined line; social: large bold text on a dark box

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: clip
description: Extract one or more frame-accurate sub-segments to separate files. Unlike trim (fast stream copy that snaps to a keyframe), clip re-encodes so cuts land exactly on the given times.

segments.description: One or more {start, end} segments; each becomes its own output file

output.description: Optional output path (single segment only; multi-segment lands under SCREENCAST_HOME/edits)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: cut_idle
description: Remove dead air: cut stretches where the screen is frozen (and, if there is audio, silent), keeping a short pad at each edge. Agent recordings are full of these pauses. dryRun reports what would be cut first. Returns the output path and the time saved.

minIdleSec.description: Only cut still stretches at least this long (default 2)

keepSec.description: Keep this much of each stretch at both edges (default 0.4)

useAudio.description: Idle only if the audio is also silent (default true when there is audio)

dryRun.description: Only report the stretches that would be cut

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: redact_region
description: Redact declared rectangles in a video so on-screen secrets are covered. This covers regions you specify; it is NOT automatic secret detection. The default style is a solid box, which is irreversible (a blur or mosaic can be partially recovered). A region that falls outside the frame is rejected rather than silently doing nothing.

start.description: Optional second to start redacting from

end.description: Optional second to stop redacting after

regions.description: One or more rectangles to redact; each may be limited to a time window

style.description: box (default) draws an irreversible solid fill; blur and pixelate are softer but partially recoverable

pad.description: Optional pixels to expand each region by, to cover anti-aliased edges (default 0)

color.description: Fill color for box style (default black)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: list_audio_devices
description: List the DirectShow audio devices ffmpeg can see on this machine and flag a likely system-audio loopback device. Use the returned name as the audio device for start_recording. System audio needs a loopback device (Stereo Mix or a virtual-audio driver); microphone capture is not supported.

name: xfade_transition
description: Crossfade two videos into one with an xfade transition. Both clips are auto-normalized to a common resolution, fps, and audio rate first, so they need not match. Audio is crossfaded when both clips have a track.

transition.description: xfade transition name (default fade): fade, wipeleft, slideup, circleopen, dissolve, ...

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: assemble_highlights
description: Stitch two or more clips into a single video, with hard cuts or an xfade transition between each. Clips are auto-normalized to a common resolution, fps, and audio rate, so they need not match.

clips.description: Two or more clip paths, in order

transition.description: 'cut' (default, hard cuts) or an xfade transition name (fade, wipeleft, slideup, ...)

duration.description: Transition length in seconds when not a cut (default 1)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: title_card
description: Generate a standalone title card: centered text on a solid background, with a silent audio track so it composes with audio-bearing clips (stitch it in with assemble_highlights). Text is rendered with a bundled font, so no system font is required.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: music_bed
description: Lay a music track under a video: the music is looped/trimmed to the video length, faded in and out, and leveled. When the video already has audio the two are mixed, optionally ducking the music under the original. The video stream is copied; only audio is re-encoded.

music.description: Path to the music audio file (looped/trimmed to the video length)

musicVolume.description: Music level 0..1 (default 0.25 over existing audio, 0.8 alone)

duck.description: Duck the music under the original audio via a sidechain (default false)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: reframe
description: Re-aspect a video to a target ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5). pad letterboxes so nothing is lost; crop fills the frame and trims the overflow.

fit.description: pad (default): scale to fit and letterbox. crop: scale to fill and center-crop.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)

name: export_preset
description: Encode a platform-ready file for youtube, instagram_reel, tiktok, x, or square. Reframes to the platform aspect, caps fps, and encodes H.264 at the platform bitrate with faststart.

platform.description: Target platform (sets aspect, resolution, fps, bitrate)

fit.description: How to fit the source into the platform aspect: pad (default) or crop

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the output path (default false)
